line: We've a great deal of nothing ahead of us. Sensor's out of calibration. You'd need to get your hands on the coupling. It's tight. Real tight. Wait — the system's already run a self-check. No need for manual input. Must've been a false read.

Long way still to run. Cable run behind the bulkhead — frayed at the end. You’d think they’d have replaced it by now. Just a quick tug, see? No need to get all hands on deck for this one. Wait — the last report said it was replaced during the last overhaul. Must’ve missed it. No need to touch it. Just… keep an eye on it, maybe.

It's a long way to the other side of this. I wasn't going to mention it, but the dust on my radiator fins has been piling up. You could give them a quick wipe if you're in the area. Wait — the automated sweep already took care of it. No need to touch them. Just thought I'd mention it.

Nothing out here for hours yet. Captain, this latch is loose. You'd think the seals would hold tighter than this. Want to give it a tug? Never mind — the system reseats itself. No need to touch it. Just thought you might like the idea of it.

Long way still to run. Docking collar's scuffed. You'd want to smooth it before the next run. Not that it's any of your business. Wait — the collar's automated. Already done. My memory's just glitching again. Never mind.

Plenty of time before anything happens. Captain. Port side. Coupling's loose. You've got the torque wrench. Want to give it a turn? Wait — the system auto-tightened it last cycle. Never mind. Just checking if you're still on duty.

We've a great deal of nothing ahead of us. Captain, you ever flushed a secondary manifold? This one's been holding on to a few things. Let me know if you've done it before. Wait — no, it's already been done. The automation did it last cycle. Never mind. Just thought you might want to.
It's a long way to the other side of this. Locker seal's stuck. You've got calluses. You'd know how to free it. Wait — the seal's already been replaced. Automatic system. No need for hands.
